title: HKDF (HMAC-based Key Derivation Function)
summary: HKDF (RFC 5869) derives keys from a shared secret. Two phases: Extract (PRK = HMAC-Hash(salt, IKM)) and Expand (OKM = T_1 || T_2 || ... where T_i = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T_{i-1} || info || i)). Used in TLS 1.3, Signal Protocol, and many modern protocols.

ext.summary: HKDF (RFC 5869) derives keys from a shared secret. Two phases: Extract (PRK = HMAC-Hash(salt, IKM)) and Expand (OKM = T_1 || T_2 || ... where T_i = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T_{i-1} || info || i)). Used in TLS 1.3, Signal Protocol, and many modern protocols.

structure.meaning: PRK = HMAC-Hash(salt, IKM). Extracts a pseudorandom key from input key material.
OKM = T_1 || T_2 || ... || T_N. T_i = HMAC-Hash(PRK, T_{i-1} || info || i). Each T_i is HashLen bytes.
Optional salt (recommended for better security). If not provided, zeros.
Input Key Material (shared secret from DH, etc.).
Output Key Material length (up to 255 * HashLen).

notes: HKDF is used in TLS 1.3 (key schedule), Signal Protocol (Double Ratchet), and many modern protocols.
HKDF is not for passwords (use Argon2/scrypt for passwords).
HKDF provides defense in depth: even if IKM is weak, the output is pseudorandom.
TLS 1.3 uses HKDF-Expand-Label with a label prefix ('tls13 ' + label).
HKDF is quantum-safe (relies on the hash function, not asymmetric crypto).
